whatFailed: POST /v2/bookings with `cal-api-version: 2026-02-25` and the documented nested `attendee` body returned 400 complaining that the flat `timeZone`, `language` and `metadata` fields are missing, because Cal.diy does not know the 2026-02-25 version and silently downgraded the route to 2024-04-15, whose input shape is a different one.

docClaim.quote: POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings. The request bodies for all 3 are almost the same except: ... For team event types it is possible to create instant meeting. To do that just pass `"instant": true` to the request body. ... Accepts different types of booking input: Create Booking (Option 1), Create Instant Booking (Option 2), or Create Recurring Booking (Option 3) ... instant: Flag indicating if the booking is an instant booking. Only available for team events. [required: start, attendee, instant] ... `awaiting_host` - an instant meeting that is live and waiting for a host to join. Create a new booking instead.

observed: Step 1, the plain non-instant booking that only sets up the flow, already 400s. Body sent: {start, attendee:{name,timeZone,email}, eventTypeId}. Response: BadRequestException with three class-validator errors, `timeZone must be a valid IANA time-zone`, `language must be a string`, `metadata must be an object`, and a `target` echo of `{start, eventTypeId}` only, i.e. the nested `attendee` object was whitelist-stripped before validation. That is the 2024-04-15 CreateBookingInput contract, not the 2024-08-13 / 2026-02-25 one the docs describe. The scenario aborted at step 1, so the instant steps 2 to 5 never ran.
impact: Documentation harm, no data loss: a self-hoster following cal.com/docs against Cal.diy gets a 400 on every v2 booking call that sends the documented version header, and the whole subject of this scenario, instant team meetings, cannot be created at all on Cal.diy because the input class, the handler and the web route were deleted by the fork.

rootCause.explanation: Two independent edition gaps stack here, and the recorded failure is caused by the first. (1) VERSION HEADER. `bootstrap.ts:33-40` installs a CUSTOM versioning extractor that returns the `cal-api-version` header only when it is a member of `API_VERSIONS`, otherwise it falls through to `VERSION_2024_04_15`, and `defaultVersion` is the same. `packages/platform/constants/api.ts:56-68` in the tested tree lists exactly 2024-06-14, 2024-06-11, 2024-04-15, 2024-08-13, 2024-09-04. `2026-02-25` is not there, so the request was routed to the 2024-04-15 BookingsController, whose input is the flat legacy shape requiring `timeZone`, `language` and `metadata` and not accepting a nested `attendee`. There is no 400 for the unknown version, the downgrade is silent, which is what turns a version mismatch into a confusing field-level validation error. (2) INSTANT BOOKINGS ARE GONE. Even on the newest version Cal.diy supports, 2024-08-13, the scenario's instant steps could not pass. `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/inputs/create-booking-input.pipe.ts:11-14` declares `CreateBookingInput = CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 | CreateRecurringBookingInput_2024_08_13`, only two shapes; the documented third, `CreateInstantBookingInput_2024_08_13`, no longer exists in `create-booking.input.ts` (the file goes straight from `CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13` at line 222 to `CreateRecurringBookingInput_2024_08_13` at line 412). The controller's own `@ApiBody` oneOf at `apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/bookings.controller.ts:139-149` lists only Option 1 and Option 2 and its description string says 'Accepts different types of booking input: Create Booking (Option 1) or Create Recurring Booking (Option 2)'. Because both validate branches run with `whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, sending `instant: true` on 2024-08-13 is rejected as an unknown property, not honoured. Beyond the DTO, `handleInstantMeeting` does not exist anywhere in the tested tree, there is no instant route under `apps/web`, and migration `20260430000000_drop_instant_meeting_webhook_trigger` removes the `INSTANT_MEETING` webhook trigger from the enum. Only vestiges remain: the `instantMeeting*` columns in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:250-253` and the `AWAITING_HOST` BookingStatus, which no Cal.diy code path can now produce through API v2.

The OTHER half, the version header, is not a regression at all: `git blame` puts the extractor at 9ad8aa981ac (Morgan, 2026-01-13, the app.ts to bootstrap.ts refactor, logic originally 0a15483c461, 2024-03-20) and the newest entry in API_VERSIONS at 5dc81e8677c (Lauris Skraucis, 2025-02-13, adding VERSION_2024_09_04). Old, correct code; what moved is the docs, which now describe versions 2026-02-25 and 2026-05-01 that only the commercial Cal.com serves.

colleagueFinding.note: Does not map to any of caldiy #1 to #5. The researcher's five cover out-of-office vs date overrides (#1), zero-length team slots (#2), a dropped 9:10 override slot (#3), seated-booking attendee oversell (#4) and unauthenticated slot-reservation mutation (#5). None touches instant bookings or the create-booking version contract. It is a clean instance of established systemic cause 1, with a second, independent edition gap underneath it.

notes: Answers to the two questions the brief asks for a systemic-cause-1 failure. (a) Would the scenario also fail on a version Cal.diy has? Partly. Step 1 would PASS on 2024-08-13: CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 requires `start` (IsDateString) and `attendee` (nested CreateBookingAttendee, name plus email or phone, timeZone), with `eventTypeId` optional-but-accepted, which is exactly the body sent, and there are no extra keys for forbidNonWhitelisted to reject. Step 2, the actual subject, would still FAIL, and differently: with `whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true` in create-booking-input.pipe.ts, `instant: true` is an unknown property and 400s as 'instant property is wrong', so there is no 201 and no `awaiting_host`. Steps 3 and 4 expect a 400 and would go green for the wrong reason (rejected as an unknown property, not as a missing-attendee or team-only violation), and step 5 is unreachable because no AWAITING_HOST booking can exist. So re-running this scenario with the header corrected would not rescue it. (b) Is there a Cal.diy-side defect in the bound doc claim independent of the version? Two contract inconsistencies, both minor and both cosmetic given the feature is gone. First, the tested controller's own ApiOperation description at bookings.controller.ts:113 still opens with 'POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings. The request bodies for all 3 are almost the same except:' while its ApiBody oneOf right below advertises only two shapes, so Cal.diy's own generated OpenAPI is self-contradictory. Second, that sentence ends on a dangling 'except:' with the instant clause stripped out, a leftover of the removal. Both are worth a one-line PR to calcom/cal.diy. Two further points for whoever triages this. The scenario's fixture `teamEventTypeInstant` (recipe.json line 463, provides id/slotStart/slotStart2/slotStart3) has no counterpart in the seed script I could find, and teams are removed from Cal.diy per README line 47, so even a version-corrected re-run has no team event type to book, which is a second reason step 2 could not have gone green. And the failure is genuinely NOT the sandbox: the 400 came back in 37 ms from a fully booted API v2 (server.stdout.txt shows the Nest route map completing), server.stderr.txt is empty, so this is a contract refusal, not a timeout or a cold start.
